The guide you are reading lives in `doc/guide` and is written in
[Quarto](https://quarto.org/){.external target="_blank"}. Any text editor will do; to build
it you need Quarto installed, see the
[Quarto get-started page](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/){.external target="_blank"}.

For the FORD-generated reference documentation of the source code see
[Documenting the Code with FORD](02_documentation.qmd).

## Previewing while you write

From the `doc` directory:

```bash
quarto preview
```

This serves the site locally and re-renders on every save, which is much faster than a full
build. `./build-doc.sh -p` renders the guide the way CI does, and `./build-doc.sh` adds the
FORD run on top.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Do not run a full build while a preview is running

`quarto preview` and `build-doc.sh` share the `doc/_site` and `doc/.quarto` state. Running a
build underneath a live preview desynchronises the preview's incremental renderer: it keeps
serving pages happily, reports "Watching files for changes", and yet silently stops picking
up your edits. If the browser disagrees with the source, suspect this first. The cure is to
stop the preview, delete `doc/_site` and `doc/.quarto`, and start it again.
:::

## Adding a page

Create a `.qmd` file in the appropriate `doc/guide` subdirectory. The sidebar is generated
automatically (`contents: auto` in `doc/_quarto.yml`), so a new file appears by itself. The
front matter controls how:

``` yaml
---
title: Authoring the ICON-Land Guide
image: /media/documentation-guide.svg
order: 3
---
```

- `title` is the sidebar entry and the page heading.
- `order` positions the page among its siblings; without it the ordering falls back to the
  file name.
- `image` is the card picture on the section landing pages, which are `listing` grids.

Because the whole page is one document, start its headings at level 1 (`#`). Section
numbering is on (`number-sections` in `doc/_quarto.yml`).

## Cross-references

Quarto resolves a reference from a label you attach to the target. Never type the number
yourself: hand-written numbers go stale the moment anything is inserted above them, and
nothing warns you when they do.

::: {.callout-important}
## References work within a page only

This is a `website` project, and Quarto cannot resolve a crossref that points into another
`.qmd`. `@sec-x` referring to a label on a different page renders as the literal text
`?@sec-x` and emits `WARNING ... Unable to resolve crossref`. To point at another page,
write an ordinary link instead, and give it the target's title as the visible text so that
it cannot silently go stale:

``` markdown
see [Documenting the Code with FORD](02_documentation.qmd)
```

Root-relative paths such as `/guide/4-developer-guide/02_documentation.qmd` also work and
survive being moved to a different depth.
:::

### Sections

Attach a label to the heading, then reference it:

``` markdown
## Vertical discretisation {#sec-vertical-discretisation}

... as defined in @sec-vertical-discretisation.
```

The label must start with `sec-`. The reference supplies the word in front of the number by
itself, so write the bare `@sec-...`:

``` markdown
as defined in @sec-vertical-discretisation      <!-- renders "Section 1.2" -->
as defined in Sect. @sec-vertical-discretisation <!-- renders "Sect. Section 1.2" -->
```

The prefix is configurable per document under `language` in the front matter, for example
`crossref-sec-prefix: "Sect."`, which is what the QUINCY scientific documentation uses. Note
that keys such as `section-prefix` at the top level of the front matter are silently ignored
by Quarto, so a prefix that looks configured may not be in effect.

### Tables

Give the table a caption line beginning with `:` and put the label there:

``` markdown
| Symbol | Description | Value |
|:-------|:------------|:-----:|
| $k_n$  | extinction coefficient | 0.11 |

: Photosynthesis parameters {#tbl-assimi:param}
```

Reference it with `@tbl-assimi:param`, which renders as "Table 2.1" and links to it. The
label must start with `tbl-`.

## Equations

Equations do **not** use Quarto's own crossref machinery here. The project applies the Lua
filter `doc/auto-subeqn.lua` (declared under `filters` in `doc/_quarto.yml`), which numbers
display equations `<chapter>.<n>` and letters the rows of a multi-line group. References are
resolved by MathJax from LaTeX labels.

### Writing an equation

Put the `\label{}` **inside** the `$$` block, and leave a blank line before the `$$`:

``` markdown
The fraction of structural N is calculated as

$$
\label{eq-veg-struc_n}
fN_{struc,cl}=k^{struc}_0-k^{struc}_1 N_{leaf,cl}
$$
```

Both details matter:

- A label written outside the block, or on the same line as surrounding text, is never seen
  by MathJax. The equation then has no anchor and every reference to it silently fails.
- Without the blank line the block is not a paragraph of its own, and the filter's handling
  of grouped equations does not apply to it.

Do not write the number into the source, and do not use Quarto's `$$ ... $$ {#eq-label}`
syntax on this site: it mixes two numbering mechanisms in one document.

### Referencing an equation

In running text use `\Eqref`, which renders as "Eq. 3.10" and links to the equation:

``` markdown
sink-limitation down-regulates photosynthesis ($\Eqref{eq-veg-growth-rate}$)
```

Where only the bare number belongs, such as the *Equation* column of a parameter table, use
`\ref`:

``` markdown
| $k_n$ | extinction coefficient | 0.11 | $\ref{eq-veg-canopy_n_distribution}$ |
```

Both must sit inside `$...$`, and each must be the whole content of its `$...$`. The filter
resolves them while the page is built: by the time it is served, a reference is an ordinary
link carrying the number as text, so it costs the browser nothing and does not depend on
MathJax having typeset the target.

Two things to avoid:

- A markdown link such as `[Eq. 3.9](#eq-veg-growth-rate)` does **not** work, and freezes
  the number at whatever was true when it was typed.
- Lowercase `\eqref` is MathJax's own macro. The filter does not rewrite it, and MathJax
  renders it as `(???)` when it cannot resolve it. Use `\Eqref`.

### Equations across several files

Unlike section and table references, equation references **do** reach other pages. The
filter records what it numbered in `doc/.eqrefs`, one file per page, and every page reads
the records the others left. Write the reference exactly as you would within a page:

``` markdown
as given by $\Eqref{eq-sb-simple-som-turnover}$
```

Two things follow from that.

A page that carries a chapter of a larger document should say which chapter it is, so that
its equations are numbered from there rather than from one:

``` yaml
---
title: Soil biogeochemistry
eq-chapter: 4
---
```

Without it the chapters are counted inside the page, which is right for a document that is
a single file, and wrong for one split across several.

And on a cold build, a page referring forwards to a page that has not been rendered yet
cannot resolve the reference. It says so, and `build-doc.sh` simply renders a second time,
which is enough. Under `quarto preview` only the file you saved is re-rendered, so numbers
on *other* pages can lag behind until a full build; the published output is always
consistent.

::: {.callout-note}
`doc/.eqrefs` is generated and is in `.gitignore`. Do not commit it: a stale record produces
a wrong number that still looks perfectly plausible, which is worse than a missing one.
:::

### Groups of equations and sub-equations

An `align` block with an outer label becomes a numbered group: the filter letters the rows
and generates a label per row by appending `_a`, `_b`, and so on.

``` markdown
$$
\label{eq-veg-growth-rate}
\begin{align}
G_C &\le G^{*}_C \\
G_N &\le \frac{k^{nut}_{labile}}{\tau_{labile}} \times N_{labile} \times dt
\end{align}
$$
```

This renders as 3.10a and 3.10b. Reference the whole group with `$\Eqref{eq-veg-growth-rate}$`
and a single row with `$\Eqref{eq-veg-growth-rate_b}$`. A row may also carry its own
`\label{}`, which is kept and numbered in sequence with its siblings.

::: {.callout-note}
## A single equation broken across lines needs `aligned`, not `align`

`align` means "several equations, number each row". If one long equation is merely wrapped
over several lines for readability, use `aligned`; the filter then gives the block one
number. With `align` every continuation line is treated as a row of its own and MathJax
reports `Multiple \tag`.
:::

## Checking your work

An equation reference that names a label which does not exist is reported by the build:

```
auto-subeqn.lua: unresolved equation reference 'eq-does-not-exist'
```

and shows up in the page as a bold `[?eq-does-not-exist]`, so it is hard to miss. Watch the
render output for those, and for Quarto's own `Unable to resolve crossref` warnings, which
are what a broken `@sec-` or `@tbl-` reference produces.

Then look at the page itself and check that every reference shows a sensible number and
that clicking it lands on the right target. Two things that only show up on screen:

- `(???)`, which means a lowercase `\eqref` slipped in;
- an equation numbered `(1)` in the middle of a lettered group, which means a row of an
  `align` block is not being numbered with its siblings.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Why the maths appears as you scroll

MathJax is configured for lazy typesetting, so equations are rendered as they come into
view. The QUINCY documentation alone holds around 1500 expressions, and typesetting them all
at once made the page slow to open. This is only safe because references are resolved at
build time; if that ever changes, lazy typesetting has to go with it, or every reference to
an equation further down the page will render as `(???)` until the reader scrolls past it.

MathJax is also pinned to a fixed version in `doc/_quarto.yml`, since the markup it produces
differs between releases. Change the pin deliberately.
:::
